articles.title: Sony’s Digital Game Ownership Argument Is Another Attack On Consumer Rights
articles.summary: As Sony marches towards its all-digital future, the company is now arguing in a class-action lawsuit that it doesn't mislead customers into purchasing digital licenses for games, instead of actual ownership of the product.
body: In a filing in California's Northern District Court made last month (and spotted by Game File ), Sony claims that "reasonable consumers would not be misled" when shopping on its storefront. The court overseeing the case against Sony is currently evaluating whether it should proceed to arbitration, as plaintiffs argue that Sony doesn't properly disclose the nature of digital purchases on its platforms.

"If you are in North America, South America, or Central America, all games and other software made available for use with your PS5 system are licensed to you, not sold, pursuant to the Software Product License Agreement."

"In the digital age, it is not plausible to allege that reasonable consumers believed they were obtaining 'ownership' of a digital game," Sony's lawyers wrote in the company's defense (via Aftermath ).

While Sony is correct that it does have disclaimers, this paints a worrying picture for the future of console games when there are no physical options available. Sony will stop producing game discs as of January 2028, and with its next-gen PlayStation console rumored to have no disc drive, the PlayStation Store will be the only game in town for accessing PS6 titles.

articles.title: YouTube Star MrBeast is Now Trying to Get Into Books, But His First Release is Reportedly 'On Track to Be a Historic Bomb'
articles.summary: YouTube star Jimmy Donaldson, better known as MrBeast, has co-written a novel — but the book has reportedly performed poorly in pre-order sales. The Most Dangerous Games, Donaldson's thriller debut written in collaboration with Alex Cross author James Patterson, is currently "on track to be a…
body: It all sounds a bit like Battle Royale meets Squid Game, which you would think would be a winning formula. But apparently there are concerns that the book's presales numbers "numbering in the four digits" is just a "tiny fraction of what th epublisher will need to justify Patterson's and YouTuber Jimmy Donaldson's hefty fees."

Herein, it seems, lies the problem. Because while the report lists The Most Dangerous Games as being "on track to be a historic bomb," presales in the single-digit thousands are typical for books of this kind, per a publishing source who spoke with IGN today. And time will tell how well the book sells over time, as Donaldson promotes it in YouTube videos, and as the lucrative end of year sales season nears. Indeed, the YouTuber has already appeared in a video titled "Read My Book, You Could Win $1,000,000", which should help sell a few more copies.

Still, publisher HarperCollins could be on the hook for a sizable sum regardless of how the book sells, depending on the advance paid to Donaldson and Patterson simply to secure the publishing rights and receive the manuscript. How much this was, we can but speculate.

articles.summary: Itagaki-san had squeezed every bit of power and performance out of Microsoft’s fledgling console, and the result was what some people believe – including me and, more importantly, our resident action-game aficionado Mitchell Saltzman – is the single greatest pure action game ever made.
body: This is an IGN opinion piece from Ryan McCaffrey, who worked at Official Xbox Magazine from 2002-2012 during the original Xbox and Xbox 360 era before joining IGN, where he remains “the Xbox guy.” In the run-up to Xbox’s 25th anniversary, he’ll be sharing his memories from the platform’s first quarter-century.

The Xbox was not always taken seriously – especially in its earliest days, and especially in Japan. “The Windows people? Making a console? They’re a software company.” No matter where you lived, if you were a gamer around the turn of the century, you remember that there was a lot to point and laugh at: the comically massive console. The absurdly large “Duke” controller (later replaced by the much better and smaller Controller S). It was… a lot.

articles.title: I Am Begging One Cool Billionaire To Take Up Double Fine’s Offer To Fund Brutal Legend 2
articles.summary: What's next for Double Fine following its split from Microsoft and Xbox? A whole lot, as the Psychonauts developer has multiple projects that it wants fans to vote on--including Brutal Legend 2, if you have a spare $100 million lying around.
body: The studio is currently seeking a more modest $400,000 on Kickstarter to fund its next project--with only a single stretch goal of $100 million--and at the time of writing, has secured $288,000 in pledges. Double Fine will be hosting its own two-week game jam called Amnesia Fortnight--not to be confused with the horror game series--and members of the studio will pitch ideas and prototype them during this period.

Company events like this led to the creation of games like Costume Quest, Iron Brigade, and Stacking, and once it's over, four of them will be chosen by Kickstarter supporters to be further developed. From that point, a single game will ultimately be chosen to be Double Fine's next project and help keep the lights on. The studio added that smaller games like these are designed to be a fun project for its team to work on, and it's still seeking funding for its next large-scale game.
So far, the Kickstarter includes the following games being prototyped, and you can click on each title to watch the pitch video.

articles.title: GTA 6 Cut This Feature Because It Was Too Real, But One Lifelike Detail Is Staying
articles.summary: Rockstar Games has confirmed more details about GTA 6, including how the developer cut a feature because it was deemed too realistic. Another feature that borrows from real life is staying, however.
body: Rockstar's Rob Nelson told Famitsu, as translated by GamesRadar, that Jason and Lucia were initially able to buy groceries and restock their fridge. However, Nelson said Rockstar decided to cut this feature because it didn't align with the studio's ideas for balancing "realism and ease of play."

"At one point during development, we were experimenting with a system that would allow you to buy groceries to restock the fridge," he said. "We had specifications for stores with groceries that you could buy and take home, and the fridge could be replenished. However, because this would have complicated the mechanics, we had to simplify it."

Presumably, this system would have tied into GTA 6's new gameplay feature where you can gain weight based on how much you eat. Players can also hit the gym to bulk up, and their physical appearance and stamina profiles will be directly related.
points: Rockstar Games has confirmed more details about GTA 6, including how the developer cut a feature because it was deemed too realistic.
Another feature that borrows from real life is staying, however.

body: I don't know about you, but my plans for the apocalypse involve hiding in a comfy bunker and playing hundreds of hours more of Paradox grand strategy games like Crusader Kings 3. And now I'll be able to play out the apocalypse during the apocalypse with the studio’s first new grand strategy game franchise since 2019's Imperator: Rome, Afterworld. Set in a not too far future North America that has been devastated by an intentionally vague cataclysm, it combines RTS and grand strategy elements as you rebuild the world in any image you desire – from terraforming to cannibalism. And that's an enticing proposition.

articles.title: Alex Ross Returns for New Marvel Dimensions Graphic Novel
articles.summary: As the artist behind monumental epics like Marvels and Kingdom Come, it goes without saying that Alex Ross is a huge name in the world of comics. In the wake of 2022's Fantastic Four: Full Circle, we're excited to see Ross crafting another original graphic at Abrams ComicArts, this time dubbed…
body: What exactly is Marvel Dimensions? That's something that Abrams has been keeping pretty well under wraps since its initial announcement. It's a book that celebrates the heroes of the Marvel Universe, but also one that pushes them in strange and unexpected directions. And it all centers around something called The In-Verse, a 32-page comic-within-a-comic that's stitched into the binding of this hardcover.

“Part of the joy of reading comics is when readers are genuinely surprised by the story on the page,” said Ross in a statement. “And that sense of mystery, suspense, and surprise is something I’ve desperately wanted to preserve for Marvel Dimensions. Every detail of the story and the design of the book has been planned extensively. My hope is that readers enjoy the unique introduction to the In-Verse as they’re transported from one world to another."
Marvel Dimensions is priced at $29.99 and is available in bookstores now. You can order a copy on Amazon.
For more, check out 6 comics to read to prepare for Marvel's Wolverine and learn more about the new Marvel horror series Midnight Spider-Man.

articles.title: The Witcher 4 Probably Won’t Be On A Disc, But Dev Teases Physical “Feelies” Of Some Type
articles.summary: CD Projekt Red recently confirmed that the long-awaited RPG The Witcher 4 is targeting a release in 2028, and that timing has led many to wonder if the Polish developer will offer the game on a disc.
body: CD Projekt joint CEO Michał Nowakowski told The Game Business that the studio has "no influence" on what companies like Sony and Microsoft choose to do with regards to supporting discs.
"The discs for the first parties, including PlayStation, have to be manufactured in their own factories. So, if they stop manufacturing indeed by 2028, then yes [we won’t have a disc]," he said.

At the same time, Nowakowski stressed that CD Projekt Red is a company that is highly fond of giving people "access to tangible collectible things." Given that, the executive teased that The Witcher 4 will, "for sure," have some kind of "box."

"We’re nerds ourselves, and we like that. We always supported that. So, whatever is the case, we’re going to be for sure having a box. We’re going to have a box that’s going to have some feelies in it," he said. "Something you’re going to be wanting to open up and enjoy. But we have no influence actually on what’s the case here."

articles.title: Ambitious New D&D Game Warlock Won’t Be a 100-Hour Open-World Slog
articles.summary: Warlock, the upcoming open-world Dungeons & Dragons video game from Invoke Studios and Wizards of the Coast, isn't going to be as long as some people may expect. That may be a good thing for gaming fans who reject open-world game bloat.
body: At Gamescom 2026, I saw an extended version of Warlock 's public gameplay demo behind closed doors. I watched the protagonist, a young woman named Kaatri, explore a small village called Crickshank, then speak with a beggar sitting on the ground. This led to her noticing a trail of blood leading inside a doorway; following it revealed a huge underground network of tunnels.

This sort of gameplay, where no two players will have exactly the same experience due to how much optional content is available, is emblematic of a vast, sprawling, 100-plus hour RPG. However, when chatting with studio head Dominic Guay afterward, he explained that Warlock actually isn't that sort of game.

"It's going to be longer than what you'd expect from a more linear game for sure, but it's not gigantic like some open worlds that are hundreds and hundreds of hours," he revealed. "One of the reasons for that is we want to have a denser open world, where you're more quickly rewarded by finding things when you explore. So we didn't want to have to draw out such far away distances that it takes forever to get to places like some other games do."
points: Warlock, the upcoming open-world Dungeons & Dragons video game from Invoke Studios and Wizards of the Coast, isn't going to be as long as some people may expect.

articles.title: Magic: The Gathering’s 10 Funniest Meme Cards of All Time, Ranked
articles.summary: As the game expands into new IPs, Wizards of the Coast has shown a growing eagerness to test the limits of just how shameless a card's visual gag can get. Marvel Super Heroes has turned some of the strangest comic panels into official Magic art, while some Secret Lair Drops in recent years have…
body: Magic: The Gathering has always had a weird relationship with the internet. The game is full of cards that were never meant to be funny but somehow became jokes among players, while new cards often even go out of their way to recreate viral memes and deeply silly pieces of pop culture. And honestly, I don’t think Magic players would have it any other way.
Whether it's an intentional crossover gag or a beautifully stupid accident, Magic has a rich history of playable punchlines. Here are the funniest meme cards to ever hit the battlefield.

Garfield's Counterspell is less of a recreation of one specific internet meme and more of a perfect translation of Garfield's entire comedic personality in Magic. Released in 2026’s Secret Lair x Garfield drop, a collection reimagining what Magic 's earliest cards might’ve looked like if Garfield had been responsible for their art, the resulting Counterspell depicts the moody cat smacking his owner, Jon, with an enormous comic-book "SLAP!" sound effect. Quite simply — and famously — Counterspell counters a target spell for only two blue mana.

articles.title: Paradox's Afterworld feels like the first grand strategy game I can properly wrap my head around
articles.summary: I've got a bit of a funny relationship with Paradox's grand strategy games. I love the idea of them, of waging and flirting my way across history on the most granular of levels.
body: Like Paradox's other in-house grand strategy games, Afterworld is looking to introduce its unique twist. So while Crusader Kings is very much the studio's take on role-playing, Afterworld draws inspiration from survival and settlement building games, letting players loose in a post-apocalyptic version of North America blighted by hazardous terrain and dangerous old-world ruins. Here, they're the guiding hand for a ragtag group of survivors, who they'll grow from humble beginnings into a continent-spanning empire - perhaps by utilising ancient technology and inspiring fear, or perhaps by building a civilisation that takes care of its people.

articles.title: The Manga Behind Netflix’s Best Horror Anime Is Officially Ending
articles.summary: One of the best horror manga in recent memory is coming to a close. The official X account for The Summer Hikaru Died has announced that the story will end in the next two chapters. Chapter 50 is scheduled for Oct. 13, while Chapter 51 is scheduled for Oct. 20.
body: For those who haven’t read the series or watched last year’s anime, it’s a queer horror story centered on two boys, Yoshiki Tsujinaka and Hikaru Indo, who live in rural Japan. Despite having very different personalities, the pair are inseparable. That is, until Yoshiki realizes something: Hikaru is no longer Hikaru. Hikaru died in a freak accident, and an unknowable entity from the mountain now controls his body. The story follows Yoshiki and "Hikaru" as they navigate a fraught relationship while trying to uncover the dark mysteries behind their small town.
points: One of the best horror manga in recent memory is coming to a close.

articles.title: Mortal Shell 2 dramatically improved in almost every way by first major update
articles.summary: On Saturday, Mortal Shell 2 received its biggest update yet, a little over a week after release. Developer Cold Symmetry was seemingly keen to address as many points of criticism as possible because the updates touch almost every aspect of the game.
body: One of Mortal Shell 2's most criticised aspects was its frugal economy. That manifested in the rate at which the game doled out various currencies, and how that limited players' ability to experiment with Shells - the game's premade classes, and weaponry.

The patch added new Tarstones which are similar to rings in Soulslikes, awarding passive and active bonuses. New Fragile Tarstones yield a Tarcore that can be used to upgrade Tarstones when they break after a certain number of uses, and new Glimpse Stones break into Glimpses after defeating a certain number of enemies.

Glimpses until now have been the game's rarest resource; the one used to increase your bond with Shells. Previously, only a limited number of Glimpses could be acquired, making it so players were never able to fully explore all Shells.

In short, Glimpses and Tarstones are no longer finite, giving players the opportunity to upgrade all Shells and Tarstones in a single playthrough. And if that's not enough, the patch also added a Shell respec item called Mether's Severance, which lets you sever your bond with a Shell, refunding all previously spent Glimpses.
points: On Saturday, Mortal Shell 2 received its biggest update yet, a little over a week after release.
Developer Cold Symmetry was seemingly keen to address as many points of criticism as possible because the updates touch almost every aspect of the game.

articles.title: CEO of Saudi Arabia's Savvy Games Group Brian Ward steps down after overseeing billions in mobile gaming acquisitions
articles.summary: Brian Ward, the CEO of the Saudi-Arabian-state-owned Savvy Games Group, has left his role. During his tenure, he oversaw $38bn of investment into various gaming companies, including Pokemon Go developer Niantic, and Monopoly Go's Scopely.
body: In a message sent to staff, verified by Bloomberg, Ward wrote: "As Savvy embarks on its next period of transformational growth, this is the right time for new leadership for that evolution". His role will be filled temporarily by Turqi Alnowaiser, deputy governor of the Public Investment Fund and Head of its International Investments Division.

Ward's run as head of Savvy Games Group had its wins and misses. The company spent $3.5bn on Niantic back in 2025 after the thunderous success of Pokémon Go, and earlier still dropped $4.9bn on Scopely, a studio best known for mobile powerhouse Monopoly Go. Savvy Games Group also invested heavily in esports, a sector that has yet to return much profit and has acted more as a marketing venture for the Saudi Arabian state through the esports world cup. Mind you, recent turbulence in the middle east resulted in the latest event to move out of Riyadh and into Paris.
points: Brian Ward, the CEO of the Saudi-Arabian-state-owned Savvy Games Group, has left his role.

body: Warhammer Age of Sigmar: Deathmaster will be available on Steam, PlayStation 5 (PS5), Xbox Series X/S, and Nintendo Switch 2 in 2027.

The team discusses the story, world, and insights into building the stealth gameplay of Warhammer Age of Sigmar: Deathmaster.
In Warhammer Age of Sigmar: Deathmaster, play as a sneaky ruthless Skaven assassin and slay your way up the ranks of the ratmen.
Warhammer Age of Sigmar: Deathmaster will be available on Steam, PlayStation 5 (PS5), Xbox Series X/S, and Nintendo Switch 2 in 2027.

body: While Grand Theft Auto 6's gameplay reveal somewhat overshadowed proceedings, it was indeed Gamescom 2026 this week and with Rich's legs giving out, it was down to John to represent us at the show. So, after dispensing with some gaming and technology news, John delivers his own "best of" tour of Gamescom, discussing the titles he loved.
